literal: Giving wealth and buying the unconsciousness of one's body indeed possesses the character of utter helplessness.
translation: To pay away one's wealth to purchase the unconsciousness of one's own body is indeed the height of foolish helplessness.
modern: பொருளைக் கொடுத்துத் தன் உடம்பை அறியாத மயக்க நிலையை விலைக்கு வாங்குவது, என்ன செய்வது என்று தெரியாத அறியாமைத் தன்மையைக் கொண்டதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet exposes the irrationality of drinking by framing it as a foolish commercial transaction. The poet describes the act of consuming alcohol as paying one's own wealth (poruḷ koṭuttu) to purchase physical unconsciousness or stupor (mey-y-aṟiyāmai koḷal). Such behavior is characterized as 'kai-y-aṟiyāmai', which denotes utter helplessness or a total lack of self-control. Through these contrasting terms of 'knowing' and 'not knowing', the verse shows how a person willingly spends resources to lose their basic physical awareness.
